title: Copernicus Sentinel-6B enters operational service
excerpt: The high-precision altimetry satellite will track global sea levels and support weather forecasting.
bodyHtml:
EUMETSAT announced that the Copernicus Sentinel-6B satellite entered operational service on October 30, 2026. Operated on behalf of the European Commission, the satellite will serve as a reference for high-precision ocean altimetry, which measures the height of the ocean surface.

The satellite provides data used by weather services to forecast conditions such as Atlantic winter storms and Mediterranean cyclones. It also monitors long-term changes in the ocean and supports maritime navigation through a high-resolution mode that measures water levels near coastlines and over inland waters. Sentinel-6B will continue a satellite record of global sea level that began in 1992.

A radio occultation instrument on board the satellite adds data on atmospheric temperature and water vapour. The satellite and its twin, Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich, will provide data on sea level across up to 95% of the ice-free ocean, along with ocean currents, wave height and wind speed, and water levels in rivers and lakes.
topic: Sentinel-6B to track rising seas, predict storms and aid forecasts
